ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a schematic diagram of the Miller-Urey experimental apparatus, with a closed gas/steam reaction area in the center; the upper part is labeled Electrical Source, indicating the use of electric sparks to simulate lightning; H2O Vapor enters from the left; Primitive Earth Gases are listed in the center, including H2O vapor, NH3, CH4, H2, CO; on the right there are outlet/return-flow descriptions related to the entering water-vapor cycle. Reasoning: The question asks which basic compound related to volcanic activity in subsequent Miller-Urey experiments does not need to be additionally added. H2S and SO2 are typical volcanic sulfur gases, and H3PO4 can serve as a phosphate/phosphorus source; all are substances that may supplement missing chemical substrates for the reaction system. By contrast, SiO2 (silicon dioxide) is mainly a component of silicate rocks/minerals, is chemically relatively inert, and is not this kind of gas-phase or reactive organic precursor supplement. Therefore, the one that does not need to be additionally added is SiO2 (silicon dioxide).

raw_record.question_text: In subsequent Miller-Urey experiments, which basic compound related to volcanic activity does not need to be additionally added?

method.method_draft: First inspect the image to identify the original setup as a sealed gas/vapor Miller-Urey apparatus with H2O vapor and primitive gases exposed to an electrical source. Then read the question/options as asking which volcano-associated compound would not be necessary to add in later versions to supply missing volcanic chemical substrates. Classify the candidate compounds by whether they are plausible reactive volcanic feedstocks for such an apparatus: H2S and SO2 are volcanic sulfur gases, H3PO4 is a phosphate source, while SiO2 is silica, an inert mineral rock component. Therefore select SiO2（二氧化硅） as the compound not needing extra addition.

method.method_draft: First inspect the diagram: the Miller-Urey chamber contains water vapor and primitive gases such as NH3, CH4, H2, and CO, energized by an electrical source. Then read the text: the issue is that missing volcanic substrates prevented formation of remaining amino acids and nucleic acids. Ask which option would not help supply elements needed for those biomolecules. Sulfur-containing volcanic compounds can help with sulfur amino acids, and phosphoric acid can help with nucleic-acid phosphate chemistry. SiO2 supplies silicon, which is not needed for amino acids or nucleic acids and is not shown as part of the gas mixture. Conclude that the compound not needing extra addition is SiO2（二氧化硅）.
